 that, however, it is pertinent to re-iterate here that during the period from 1992 till date, no return was approved by the respondent No.2. Summary of Share Capital was filed before the respondent No.2 for the year 2010-2012; however those were not approved by the respondent No.2. Moreover, no Particulars of Directors of the respondent No.1 company was filed before the respondent No.2 after 1991; that in the meantime Mr. Hassan Dawood died on 14.08.2013 and hence, there are only two directors in the company, namely the petitioner and the respondent No. 3; that the respondent No.1 company is being run defying most of the provisions of the Companies Act, 1994. The respondent No. 1 company had no valid annual general meetings after 1991. None of the Returns submitted after 1991 was approved by the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies. The purported audit reports submitted before the respondent No. 2 for the years 1996, 2008- 2012 are ex-facie illegal. The Audit Reports of the respondent No.1 Company for the year  

 4. Although a Vokalatnama has been filed on behalf of the respondent No. 1 and 3, but no affidavit in-opposition has been filed on behalf of the respondent No. 1 and 3 controverting the allegations made in the petition for winding up.  

 5. The learned Advocate Mr. Ahsanul Karim, appearing along with learned advocate Mr. Mr. Khairul Alam Chowdhur, Mr. Shamim Ahmed Mehedi and Ms. Farzana Khan, for the petitioner and having placed the petition along with the documents annexed, submits that that the respondent No. 1 company did not hold any AGM from the year 2008 to 2009. Besides, without obtaining any condonation of delay from the Hon'ble High Court Division, the respondent No, 1 company held purported AGM for the years 2010, 2011 and 2012. Moreover, no Particulars of Directors of the respondent No. 1 company was filed in the office of the respondent No. 2 (RJSC) after 1991. He also submits that Mr. Hassan Dawood, one of the directions, died on 14.08.2013. Hence, at present there are only two directors in the company, namely the petitioner and the respondent No. 3. He further submits that the respondent No.1 Company is being run defying the provisions of the Companies Act, 1994. The respondent No.1 Company held no annual general meetings after 1991 in as much as in the absence of quorum no valid AGM a can be held or conducted. None of the Returns submitted after 1991 was approved by the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Finns. No proper audit was done in the respondent No.1 Company from 1992 till date. The purported audit reports submitted before the respondent No.2 for the years 1996, 2008-2012 are ex -facie illegal. He next submits that the respondent No.3 is acting as the Managing Director of the company from 1992 till date. But, section 110 of the Companies Act, 1994 prohibits appointment or employment of any individual as a Managing Director of a company for more than 5 years, whereas the respondent No. 3 is continuing his office as the Managing Director for more than 20 years. Pursuant to sections 95 and 96 of the Act, the respondent No. 1 company was liable to hold Board meetings at least once in every three months and at least-four times a year and the notice of such board meeting ought to have been communicated in writing to the petitioner. The petitioner was inserted as a shareholder and is a director of the respondent No.1 Company from the year 2008 and in spite of so, in the last 6 years, the petitioner never received any notice of the, Board Meeting or of any general meeting. No board meeting or general meeting can be validly held without the petitioner, since presence of 2(two) directors members or, as the case may be is required to form quorum for such meeting. Hence, the vokalatnama purportedly executed by the respondent No. 3 on behalf of the respondent No. 1 (company) is not valid execution. He was not authrised in any board meeting to represent the company in this matter. So, he submits, the respondent No. 1 cannot be treated as present in this matter. Besides, he continues, the respondent No.3 is running the company and taking decisions therein illegally and without any approval obtained in any Board meeting or any General Meeting. He is submitting no statutory reports and running the affairs of the company as it is his proprietorship concern. As such, he argues, evidently, respondent company has ceased to be a going concern and the substratum of the company has gone. He further submits that the respondent No. 3 did not file any affidavit-in-opposition controverting the allegations made in the petition and thus admitted the facts stated in the petition. Hence, the respondent No. 1 company is liable to be wound up in the facts and circumstances of this case.  

 6. The learned advocate for the respondent No. 3 Mr. Md. Moimur Alum Khan has found it difficult to controvert the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the petitioner. He has rather placed a petition for compromise, jointly signed by and on behalf of the petitioner and the respondent No. 3 and prayed for a compromise decree accordingly.  

 8. The submissions of the learned advocates referred to in the arguments are substantiated by the materials on record. In other words, them is no materials on record to show that the respondent-company held any AGM for the years 2008 and 2009 or for the years 2010, 2011 and 2012, with condonation of delay granted by this Court. Besides, it appears that, Mr. Hassan Dawood, and Mr. Md Hassain Innath (MD) were shown as directors of the company. It is stated in the petition and not denied that Mr. Hasan Dawood died on 14.08.2013. Petitioner is his daughter. Her induction in the Board in 2008 is not denied by the respondent. As such, at present, there are two directors in the company, namely, the petitioner and the respondent No. 3. No quorum for board meeting or any general meeting can be formed in the absence of the petitioners in as much presence 2(two) directors or members, as the case may be, is required to hold such meeting, vide Article 34 and Article 20 of the Articles of Association (Annexure-A2). There is no material on record to show that any notice of board meeting or of any general meeting was served upon the petitioner since she was inducted to the board in the year 2008, although section 95 and 96 of the Act requires that notice of each board meeting shall be served upon all director, and the company must hold at least 4 board meetings in each year. Besides, the provisions of section 81 of the Act requires holding of AGM each year. Similarly, there, is no material on record to show that the tenure of the respondent No. 3 as the Managing Director was ever extended since 1992 till date. As per provisions of section 110(3) of the Act, he has ceased to be Managing Director of the respondent-company in 1992. In the record there is no material to show that any auditor was appointed in any AGM or that any audit was done since 1992 till date or was submitted for consideration in any AGM. There is no material, as well, on record to show, which is the burden of the respondent No. 3, that the Registrar, Joint Stock Companies and Finns has obtained any return submitted after 1991.  

 9. Hence, I find that the respondent company has lost its corporate character and has ceased to be a going concern. It has lost its substratum. It is being run as if it is a sole proprietorship concern. Besides, the power exercised by the respondent No. 3, describing him as Managing Director, after expiry of his tenure is also unauthorized.  

 10. The company has violated the provisions of section 94, 95, 81 and 110 of the Act for not holding board meetings and Annual General Meetings and for not holding any AGM and for not submitting any statutory return, as required by law.  

 12. It further appears that the petitioner and the respondent No. I and 3 have entered into a compromise and accordingly filed a joint application sworn on 13.7.2014. In the said application it has been stated that the petitioner-applicant No.1 (hereinafter referred to as the petitioner), the respondent No.1- applicant No.2 (hereinafter referred to as the respondent No.1) and the respondent No.3- applicant No.3 (hereinafter referred to as the respondent No.3) have filed this instant application, jointly, for passing an order in terms of the Compromise Agreement dated 09.072014, executed amongst the petitioner, as the first party, and the respondent Nos. 1 and 3, jointly, as the second party; that the petitioner filed the instant Company Matter under section 241 read with section 245 of the Companies Act, 1994 read with Rules 8 and 263 of the Companies Rules, 2009 for winding up of the respondent No. 1 company. The High Court Division, vide order dated 18.05.2014, was, pleased to admit the said application and fixed the matter for hearing on 13.07.2014; that in the meantime, the respondent Nos.1 and 3 received the notice of the said Company.  (9.) That the parties agree that if Mr. Md. Hassan Imam fails to pay the entire amount of Tk. 55,00,00,000.00 (Taka fifty five crore) only within 3 (three) months of execution of this agreement, then the said Company Matter No. 167 of 2014 shall revive and the parties hereby accord their consent that the Hon'ble High Court Division shall pass an order of winding up of Hassan Movies Limited by appointing a liquidator (who shall be a reputed Chartered Accountant Finn), who shall distribute the-assets of the company to Ms. Aysha Dawood and Mr. Md. Hassan Imam as per ratio of their shareholding in Hassan Movies Limited. 

  (11) That Ms. Aysha Dawood shall arrange an undertaking from her mother Ms. Dilruba Dawood to the effect that the said Ms. Dilruba Dawood has no claim, whatsoever, in Hassan Movies Limited. (12.) That this agreement is executed in 3 (three) counter-parts, I (one) copy for each party and the rest is to be submitted before the Hon'ble High Court Division in Company Matter No. 167 of 2014 along with the application for compromise. (13.) That the parties agree to submit this compromise agreement before the Hon'ble High Court Division of Supreme Court of Bangladesh in Company Matter No. 167 of 2014 to be recorded by Hon'ble High Court-Division in the said Company Matter to the satisfaction of the Hon'ble Court under Order )0C111, Rule 3 of the Code of Civil 'Procedure and thereby the parties shall jointly file an application under Order XXIII Rule 3 of Code of Civil Procedure read with Rule 8 and Rule 263 of Companies Rules, 2009 for disposing of the above Company Matter No. 167 of 2014, subject to terms and conditions of this Compromise Agreement on recording the terms and conditions of this Compromise Agreement to the satisfaction of the said Hon'ble Court. The parties in their joint application shall pray for an order in terms of this Agreement. 

 13. In the Compromise Agreement dated 09.07.2014 (marked as Annexure "W"); it is recorded, that according to clause 13 of the said Compromise Agreement, the parties agreed to file an application jointly under Role 8 and Rule 263 of Companies Rules, 2009 for passing an order by this Court in terms and conditions of this Compromise Agreement to resolve the contentions between the parties outside Court as agreed in the Compromise Agreement. It was further agreed between the parties, as stipulated in clause 9, that if Mr. Md. Hassan Imam fails to pay the entire amount of Tk. 55,00,00,000.00 (Taka fifty five crore) only within 3 (three) months of execution of this agreement, then the said Company Matter No. 167 of 2014 shall revive and the parties also agreed that the High Court Division will pass an order of winding up of Hassan Movies Limited by appointing a liquidator (who shall be a reputed .Chartered Accountant Firm), who shall distribute the assets of the company to Ms. Aysha Dawood and Mr. Md. Hassan Imam as per ratio of their shareholding in Hassan Movies Limited as per Compromise Agreement dated 09.07.2014 and prayed that in the situation stated above, this Court may be pleased to pass an order in terms of the said Compromise Agreement dated 09.07.2014; otherwise the applicants Shall suffer irreparable loss.  

 14. The learned advocate for the petitioner and the learned advocate Mr. Md. Monzur Alam Khan, appearing for the respondent No. 1 and 3, referring to the agreement, submits that the parties have entered into an amicable settlement in terms of an agreement dated 9.7.2014 signed amongst the petitioner and the respondent No. I and 3 and have filed an application for passing a decree on compromise, as per the terms and conditions by incorporated in the compromise agreement and as agreed between the parties. The said agreement has been annexed as Annexure-W to the compromise petition.  

 15. Heard the learned advocates and perused the application for compromise decree along with the substantive petition and the materials on record. I find merit in the petition. In result, the petition is allowed. The petitioner company, namely Hassan Movies Limited, incorporated on 19.12.1962, is hereby wound up form the date the petition has been presented on 18.05.2014, subject to the following directions that-(1) the petitioner or his advocate shall send to the Registrar of Companies a notice of this order, in Form No. 18, to enable him to notify the Official Receiver about this judgment and order, as required by Rule 75 of the Companies Rules, 2009. (since the Official Receiver himself is not appointed as the liquidator.) 

 (2) Mr. Moksadul Islam, learned advocate of 3A, Sonartori Tower, 12, Sonargaon Road, Banglamotor, Dhaka-1000 and a member of the Supreme Court Bar Association, is hereby appointed as "the Official Liquidator of Hasan Movies" (hereinafter referred to as the company), as per section 255(1) of the Act read with Rule 76 of the Companies Rules, 2009. (3) The Official Liquidator is hereby directed - (i) to advertise, as required by Rules 76 and 133, the order of liquidation to submit claims giving 14 days’ time, with adequate proof (vide Rules 133 to 147), from the claimants, if any, in two national daily newspapers, one in English and another in Bangle, in the locality where the registered office or the principal place of business of the company is situated. (ii) to inform this order of winding up by issuing notice upon the company, as required by Rule 77 (since company is not the petitioner and did not appear in this matter), (iii) to open a bank account with Sonali Bank, Supreme Court Branch, in the name of the "Official Liquidator of Hassan Movies Limited (in liquidation)", as required by Rule 103, (iv) to maintain all books, records and accounts as required under the provisions of the Companies Act and the Rule 110 of the Companies Rules,' 2009 showing all assets and liabilities of the company. (v) to submit quarterly reports, of the accounts of the company, to the court, till it's dissolution or otherwise ordered by this court. (vi) to exercise his powers and discretion, vested in him under section 262 of the Act, with due regard being had to interest of the company, its creditors and contributories and subject to the control of the court. (vii) to prepare and to furnish before this court a list of all contributories (subject to this court's right to rectify the same, if so required according to law) (viii) to submit his statement/report, further and/or supplementary statement/reported, to this court, as required by section 259 of the Act, read with Rules 119 and 120, as soon as practicable upon receiving the statement of affairs to be filed under section 258(since winding up order is made). (4) The Official Liquidator is directed to take into custody all movable and immovable properties of the company, if any, (by making an inventory). including the title deeds and to dispose of the same, as permitted by section 262 of the Act, with prior sanction of this court (vide Rules 168 to 170), and to use the sale proceeds, if any, towards settling the liabilities of the petitioner company, if any, in the manner prescribed by Rules 148 to 162 and regard, being had to the provisions of section 325 concerning preferential payment as well as to show separately the list of secured and unsecured creditors, if any, giving their name, particulars and the amount of their claim, in two columns, one showing the principal sum and another showing the interest, if any, the last column showing the total seem claimed. He shall, to that end, submit application accordingly for disbursement of the assets, to allow the cost and expenses incurred and also showing the assets, liabilities cash, if any at hand. (5) The respondent No. 3, on behalf  of the company is directed to submit verified statements of affairs in duplicate, signed by him, and counter signed by the petitioner,. official liquidator, as required under the provisions of section 258 of the Act, within 21 (twenty-one) days from the date of winding up order or from the date of sending this record to company section, whichever is occurred later (Since no provisional liquidator is appointed in this case). (6) The respondent No. 3, being the in person in control of the affairs of the company shall furnish the name of all bankers of the company, giving account numbers, enclosing statement of accounts, name of the signatories and also enclosing authenticated copies of the resolution regarding operation of the bank accounts, within the time limit prescribed in the proceeding paragraph, to the official liquidator. (7) The person named at preceding paragraph No. (6) and/or the official in charge of the estate, if any, of the company shall give particulars of and Landover all title deeds of all immovable and movable properties of the company (if any) to the official liquidator within such time limit as prescribed in the proceeding paragraph and (8) Since the Official Liquidator is permitted by law to take into custody all assets and properties of his company, as per provisions of section, 262, so the concerned bank manager(s) and, in which account of Hassan Movies Ltd is being maintained or was maintained the Managing Director(s) is/are directed to open a bank account in the name of official liquidator and to hand over specimen card, forthwith on demand being made, to the official liquidator to transfer the amount to the account maintained by the official liquidator, on his signing necessary papers, and also to hand over cheque book so that the official liquidator can bear all necessary cost and expenses incurred in the process of winding up and to pay the salaries, rents, bills, wages etcetra, if any or to supply true copies of all documents concerning the accounts of the said company, if the account is already closed. These banks shall not honour any instrument, nor shall carry out any instruction, other than that signed/made by the official liquidator. Banks shall not be discharged from its ability otherwise, to the company or any other parties to who it owes any obligation.(9) The respondent No. 3, on behalf of the company, shall submit an affidavit of compliance as regards directions Nos. 5 to 7 within one week thereafter. (10) The Company and respondent No. 3, the members of the board, all shareholders/contributors are hereby restrained from operating bank accounts, to remove or transfer or encumber any moveable or immovable properties of the company including, but not limited to, the vehicles, equipment, machineries etcetra of the company and not to remove any documents without leave of the court, from the date the winding up order is deemed to have commenced. - (11) The official Liquidator shall follow and comply with all such provisions as are laid down in the Act and the Rules and as are applicable in the process of winding up and he shall be solely responsible for the default, if any, committed in the process of winding up. He shall not withdraw any amount more than that as may be required to meet the lawful and reasonable cost and expenses and/or to settle the lawful claims and/or to distribute the surplus assets amongst the contributories, if any, as per law and with prior sanction of the court. Besides, he shall bring, in writing, to the knowledge of the court all facts that are material to ensure compliance of the provisions law and to protect-interest of the creditors, claimants, contributories and the company, as the case may be.
